clue.text: Step outside a lot of rich people

indicators.note: the word for a step goes around the trimmed word for rich, so outside signals the container

parts.note: a pace is a step

indicators.note: a lot of a word, but not all, means its tail is cut off here

parts.note: opulent means rich

explanation.surface: Someone steps out of a crowd of wealthy folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' signals a trimmed synonym: most of the word for rich, minus its last three letters, sits inside the step.
explanation.definitionFit: The populace is the common people of a place, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Warning of accident — hence time taken to catch criminals?

definitions.text: Warning of accident — hence time taken to catch criminals?

parts.words: Warning of accident — hence time taken to catch criminals?
parts.note: reads first as a roadside sign after a crash, then as a jibe that the force takes ages to make arrests

explanation.definitionFit: A roadside sign telling drivers to go slowly after an accident, reread as a comment on slow policing.

clue.text: Condescended to, not praised, maybe as Johnson by 4

indicators.note: maybe suggests the words could be arranged differently, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Treated with condescension rather than praise, as Samuel Johnson was by a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as Johnson by 4' adds colour: Lord Chesterfield offered Dr Johnson belated patronage of his Dictionary, which Johnson scorned.
explanation.definitionFit: To patronise someone is to treat them with condescension, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Feudal superior for Walloons?

parts.note: a lord to whom vassals owe service, and also a Belgian city in French-speaking Wallonia

explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a feudal lord, and Liège is a major city of the Walloon region of Belgium.

clue.text: 8 that was 22 23's

definitions.meaning: a deep-buttoned sofa is a kind of seat
the Derbyshire constituency the politician represented in Parliament

explanation.definitionFit: A chesterfield is a padded sofa, and Chesterfield was the parliamentary seat the politician held from 1984.

clue.text: Pitiful affair of the quiet musketeer

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
Athos is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers

explanation.surface: A sad episode in the life of the least talkative of the Musketeers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality that arouses pity, so a pitiful affair is a fair loose description.

clue.text: Hill dweller runs away to Bucks, perhaps

parts.note: an ant lives in an anthill
to elope is to run away to marry

explanation.surface: A mountain resident flees to the county of Buckinghamshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bucks' looks like the county (Buckinghamshire), but it means male deer or antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Male antelopes are called bucks, so bucks are an example of the animals.

clue.text: Expect to follow boy in 16 for 4's name

definitions.text: to follow boy in 16 for 4's name
definitions.meaning: placed after Stan, the boy's name at the start of the 16 answer, it makes Stanhope, the family name of the Earls of Chesterfield

explanation.definitionFit: Hoping is expecting with desire; and Philip Stanhope was the Lord Chesterfield of Johnson's day.

clue.text: How one is on a horse determines the throne

definitions.text: How one is on a horse
definitions.meaning: a rider's ... is their posture in the saddle

explanation.definitionFit: A rider's seat is their position in the saddle, and a throne is a ceremonial seat.

clue.text: Remove my blindfold for a consideration

definitions.meaning: a blindfolded person would ask to be allowed to look
the phrase is what one says while thinking something over

explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase asks to be allowed to look; idiomatically it is said while pausing to consider.

clue.text: More work for adults covered by posh headgear

indicators.note: the adults' letter sits under the hat, so in an across light it follows it

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage, so posh
a topi is a sun helmet
A is the film certificate for adults

explanation.surface: Grown-ups wearing smart hats seem to be doing extra work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is Sir Thomas More, not 'extra'; his best-known work is the book that gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is the 1516 book by Sir Thomas More describing an ideal island state.

clue.text: 4 feature forms piers

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: a bent version of one word rearranges into the other

explanation.surface: Something characteristic of the sofa rearranges supports.
explanation.walkthrough: Chesterfield's church has a famous twisted spire; read as wordplay, 'crooked' scrambles SPIRE into PIERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The twisted spire of St Mary and All Saints is the best-known landmark of the town of Chesterfield.

clue.text: Trainer retaining Piggott — non-starter — one doesn't want too much of this

definitions.text: one doesn't want too much of this

indicators.note: the trimmed word for trainer holds the jockey's first name inside it
a non-starter here is a word losing its first letter

parts.note: a school trains its pupils
Lester Piggott was a famous British jockey

explanation.surface: A racehorse trainer keeps on Lester Piggott, who fails to start, and the result is unwelcome excess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trainer' suggests racing, but it is SCHOOL; 'non-starter' removes its S to leave CHOOL, which holds LESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholesterol is a fatty substance in the blood that people try to keep at a low level.

clue.text: Piece of comedy could be a riot in new group

indicators.note: the shuffled riot goes inside the reshaped group
new means the letters are put in a fresh order
could be signals that the letters may form something else

explanation.surface: A slapstick sketch might cause uproar among a newly formed troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' turns A RIOT into ATORI, placed in PURGO, the reshuffle of GROUP from 'new'. 'Comedy' is Dante's Divine Comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Purgatorio is the second of the three parts of Dante's Divine Comedy.

clue.text: L for your address and phone number?

definitions.text: L for your address and phone number?

parts.words: L for your address and phone number?
parts.note: the letter L is the head of the word for a written message, and the printed heading of notepaper carries your contact details

explanation.definitionFit: A letterhead is the printed heading on stationery giving name, address and phone number.

clue.text: Cantonese?

parts.note: read not as the Chinese dialect but as people of the cantons, the regions of an Alpine country

explanation.definitionFit: Switzerland is divided into cantons, so its people could whimsically be called canton-folk.

clue.text: Awful snag in politics, so 22 23 gave it up

indicators.note: the scrambled snag sits inside the word for politics

parts.note: the state is the political body or sphere of government

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters are in a dreadful mess

explanation.surface: A terrible hitch in public life led the politician to renounce something.
explanation.walkthrough: The politician inherited the title Viscount Stansgate in 1960 and renounced it in 1963 to stay in the Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: Stansgate was the peerage the politician disclaimed, giving up the title to sit as an MP.

clue.text: To give radical treatment maybe I should abandon our protein

indicators.note: dropping a letter from the pool of words and rearranging the remainder signals the composite

parts.note: the letters to be reshuffled once the I goes

explanation.surface: A dietary instruction: drop me from our protein for a drastic regime.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of OUR PROTEIN minus I are rearranged; 'radical' means of the root, so cutting back roots is literally radical treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: To root-prune a plant is to cut its roots, which is literally a radical (root) treatment.

clue.text: Worker working on musical show nearly backed another

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter of the word for a musical show is dropped

parts.note: an opera is a musical stage show

indicators.note: backed means the second show's title is read from the end

parts.note: Evita is another musical show, by Lloyd Webber

explanation.surface: An employee is busy on one stage show and nearly backs a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' is a second definition (operative means working) and 'on' joins; OPER plus ATIVE, which is EVITA reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: An operative is a worker, especially a factory hand or a secret agent.

clue.text: Vision may be jolly

definitions.meaning: as in 'a ... better', meaning a jolly good deal better

explanation.definitionFit: Sight means eyesight, and colloquially 'a sight' intensifies like 'jolly' in 'a sight better'.

clue.text: Being no crank, I need no one else to get me going

definitions.text: Being no crank, I need no one else to get me going

parts.words: Being no crank, I need no one else to get me going
parts.note: reads as a sensible person who motivates themselves, but also as a car engine that needs no starting handle

explanation.definitionFit: A self-starter is both an ambitious person needing no prompting and the electric motor that replaced the crank handle on cars.

clue.text: Flying is dreadful

definitions.meaning: on the wing, in the air

explanation.definitionFit: Awing means on the wing, and also inspiring awe, which is close to dread.

clue.text: Spooner's Napoleon X, now a political institution

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starts of words, so the opening sounds trade places

parts.note: Boney was the British nickname for Napoleon
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Napoleon's Tenth, once a regiment, has become an established body.
explanation.walkthrough: BONEY TEN with first sounds exchanged is heard as TONY BENN, the Labour politician later treated as a national institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Benn, the veteran Labour politician, had by then become a cherished national figure, a political institution.

clue.text: See 22
There's never anything fresh in the system

indicators.note: the fresh thing goes inside the letters for never

parts.note: never is no (O) plus ever (AY, an old word for ever)
something fresh is new

explanation.surface: A complaint that nothing new ever comes into the organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never' is read as 'no ever', with the old poetic word for ever. A one-way system is a traffic scheme where streets run in one direction only.
explanation.definitionFit: One-way describes a traffic system in which vehicles may travel in only one direction.

clue.text: Fine work horse reportedly European without monarch

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for a young horse is taken as heard

parts.note: a filly is a young female horse

indicators.note: without tells us the king's letter is removed from the nationality

parts.note: a Greek is a European
K is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A fine piece of craftsmanship: a horse, so they say, belonging to a European who has lost their king.
explanation.definitionFit: Filigree is delicate ornamental work of fine wire, so it is literally fine work.

clue.text: There's poor Rodney

definitions.note: the definition is there; the 's joins it to the wordplay

indicators.note: poor suggests the name is in a bad way, so its letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Pointing out poor old Rodney over there.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old word meaning over there, at a distance.

clue.text: China also dropped by 22 23

definitions.meaning: A famous make of English pottery
the politician was born Anthony ... Benn and dropped the middle name

explanation.definitionFit: Wedgwood is fine English porcelain, and also the middle name the politician stopped using.
